subject: Request: concise subprocessor manifest & country-summary for procurement review
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finlex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
Date: 2029-05-17T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: concise subprocessor manifest & country-summary for procurement review

Hi Marta,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As FinLex progresses through procurement, Legal and Procurement have asked for a short, machine-friendly manifest of third parties you rely on that will handle customer data for the integration (we're focusing on telemetry, transit, and short-term cache layers).

Can you please send a single CSV that lists each subprocessor, the role (e.g., telemetry, transit, storage), the primary country where processing occurs, whether they handle raw payloads or only aggregated/metadata, and the KMS/jurisdiction (if applicable)? A one-page country-summary (countries touched + high-level encryption note) would be very helpful for our legal team.

If you already have SOC2/external certifications or a brief evidence pack, please attach stubs (PDF/S3 link). We're trying to keep this ask compact for procurement review — one CSV and one short PDF or zipped evidence set.

Target timeline: can you share this by EOD tomorrow (Fri)? If not, an ETA is fine.

Thanks,

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
s: +1 (415) 555-0192
redwood.inference

Subject: Re: Request: concise subprocessor manifest & country-summary for procurement review

Hi Sergio,

Attached is a compact manifest and our SOC2 snapshot. The CSV has columns as requested: name, role, country_primary, data_scope (raw|hashed|aggregated), kms_jurisdiction. Quick notes:
- Most telemetry flows through EdgePulse (Ireland) and is encrypted at rest using our EU KMS (key managed in EMEA).
- Transit proxies occasionally route to US-based analytics for aggregated metrics only.
- No subprocessors have access to customer-supplied raw PII for the default integration (unless customer enables detailed debug logs).

Files attached:
- finlex_subprocessors_manifest_20290517.csv (CSV)
- finlex_soc2_snapshot_2029-01.pdf (PDF, redacted)

Let us know if you need a more detailed chain-of-custody map.

Best,

Date: 2029-05-17T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: concise subprocessor manifest & country-summary for procurement review

Sergio / Lauren,

Thanks for the ping and thanks Marta for the quick turnaround.
A few clarifying asks from our side (Legal & Privacy):

- Can you confirm which subprocessors (if any) perform tokenization or deterministic hashing of user content? Legal needs to know if tokens are reversible and where the token/key material is stored.
- For the US-based analytics path you mentioned, can you provide whether PKI/TLS termination occurs in the US and whether logs contain customer identifiers? If logs are stripped to aggregates, please say so explicitly.
- If EdgePulse (Ireland) is the primary telemetry collector, does FinLex have an onshore/EU-only routing flag for EU customers? If yes, please indicate the operational controls.

Also, please attach the DPA addendum draft you use for reserve processing limits — we can start a quick review and send a DocuSign link once terms are agreed.

Quick one-line replies are fine; Procurement wants the CSV and snapshot for now but Legal needs these clarifications before sign-off.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finlex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
Date: 2029-05-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: concise subprocessor manifest & country-summary for procurement review

Marta — looping back. Marissa flagged a few specific legal clarifications; I've drafted a short note below that you can forward to your ops team or answer inline.

- Tokenization: does FinLex ever store reversible tokens for customer payloads? (yes|no). If yes, where are the key stores and who holds the KMS admin role?
- US analytics path: are customer identifiers present in logs sent to the US? (yes|no) If 'no', confirm logs are aggregated and show an example field list.
- EU-only routing: do you support a per-customer onshore routing toggle? If so, how is it implemented (network tag, tenant flag, region selection)?

If it's easier, feel free to sign the attached DPA addendum draft (we attached a Redline) and we'll send a DocuSign envelope. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/example-link-abc123

Thanks again for the fast help here — procurement is hoping to close the PO next week.

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Sent from Redwood Inference]
